title.narrative: Women, men, youth and vulnerable groups enjoy full realization of rights at work

description.narrative: The CPO KHM128 addresses the critical challenges faced by Cambodian migrant workers, particularly the lack of safe and legal migration pathways and the persistent risks of exploitation, especially in sectors like fishing and seafood processing. Despite policy advancements and mechanisms introduced by the Cambodian government, including a third Labour Migration Policy and formal complaint systems, many migrants, over 1.1 million as of 2020, the majority of whom are women, continue to depend on informal brokers due to the cost and complexity of legal migration channels. The CPO aims to strengthen the governance of labour migration by supporting the development of gender-responsive and disability-inclusive migration policies that offer greater protection and opportunity for all migrant workers. The primary beneficiaries of this initiative are migrant workers themselves, particularly women, who often face the greatest barriers to safe migration and decent work. Families and communities that rely on remittances, as well as Cambodian institutions, recruitment agencies, and civil society organizations, also stand to benefit. The strategy is carried out in collaboration with key partners, including international organizations such as the ILO, IOM, and UNDP, and national bodies like the Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training. Expected outcomes for the biennium include the drafting of a revised Labour Migration Law, strengthened capacity of recruitment agencies and tripartite actors, and expanded access to services. This includes safer migration options, skills training for women, and digital tools such as the Saver Asia app. Through these actions, the programme seeks to ensure that migration becomes a safer, fairer, and more empowering option for Cambodian workers.
